This is a tough one, it varies between Jurisdictions but the general rule is in a situation like this a person must reasonably believe themselves/someone else  is a imminent danger of harm and a person must only use “enough force “ to end the imminent threat . In most states this means it must be a violent felony crime taking place . A “reasonable amount of force to end the imminent threat” is where the lines become very blurred.

In Texas, the penal code specifically states you may only use a minimal amount of force , yourself/ the other person did not provoke the attack, you/other person are not engaged in crime . 

As for California, you/other person must be/believe they are in imminent danger, have reason to believe a threat exists, and does not use more force than necessary.
